event_name: MOPAR NHRA Las Vegas Nationals powered by Dodge

pairs.note:
Antron Brown is 15 - 9 in Rd. 1 when starting 10th in the field.Brown's overall record at this event
is 27 - 23 (21 - 16 in TF). By round, his record is 14 - 11 in Rd. 1, 8 - 6 in Rd. 2, 3 - 5 in Rd. 3,
and 2 - 1 in the Final. He won this race in 2013 (Beat C. Millican) and 2020 (Beat S. Torrence), and
was runner-up here in PSM in 2001 (Lost to S. Gann). He has qualified in the top half of the field at
14 of his 25 races here. His lowest starting spot at this event is #13 (2003 in PSM and 2012 in TF).
He is 6 - 3 in the Countdown this year.

Maddi Gordon lost to Antron in the final round at Dallas.  

Brown is 2 - 1 against Gordon in prior events. 

Brown with the starting line advantage and never trailed for the win.  He makes his quickest pass of
the weekend.  Antron Brown's MOV: 0.0178 seconds (approximately 9 feet).

Gordon with her quickest and fastest pass of the weekend in the losing effort.  She has a big top end
speed and sets the track speed record.

Justin Ashley is 6 - 4 against Millican in Rd. 1 overall (1 - 1 this year).  Ashley's overall record
at this event is 9 - 7. By round, his record is 5 - 2 in Rd. 1, 3 - 2 in Rd. 2, 1 - 2 in Rd. 3, and 0
- 1 in the Final. He was runner-up here in 2023 (Lost to M. Salinas). His lowest starting spot at
this event is #14 (2019). He has qualified in the top half of the field at 5 of his 7 races here and
is 4 - 4 in the Countdown this year.

In his last 10 races Clay Millican is 3 - 7 in Rd. 1.  Millican's overall record at this event is 16
- 20. By round, his record is 12 - 8 in Rd. 1, 3 - 9 in Rd. 2, 1 - 2 in Rd. 3, and 0 - 1 in the
Final. He was runner-up here in 2013 (Lost to A. Brown) and has qualified in the top half of the
field at 8 of his 22 races here. His lowest starting spot at this event is #15 (2005 and 2023). He
DNQ here in 2006 and 2014, and is 1 - 4 in the Countdown this year.

Ashley with the starting line advantage and the power to hold on for the hole shot win in a close
one.  Justin Ashley's MOV: 0.0027 seconds (approximately 16 inches).

Ashley dropped cylinders right in the lights and it pushed him over by the centerline, but he held on
for the win.

Shawn Langdon's 48 round wins this year are the most for him since 2013 (54).  Langdon's overall
record at this event is 14 - 17. By round, his record is 9 - 8 in Rd. 1, 4 - 5 in Rd. 2, 1 - 3 in Rd.
3, and 0 - 1 in the Final. He was runner-up here in 2025 (Lost to B. Force). He has qualified in the
top half of the field at 12 of his 17 races here. His lowest starting spot at this event is #16
(2011). He has set Low E/T at 8 races this year and is 14 - 1 in the Countdown this year. 

Cameron Ferre is making his 52nd start.   The #16 TF qualifier has never won a round at this event.
Ferre's overall record at this event is 0 - 4. This is his 9th race this year and his 1st race here
since 2022.

Langdon is 4 - 0 against Ferre in prior events. 

Ferre with a slight starting line advantage, but Langdon had the lead by the time they go by the
Christmas tree and never trailed from there on for the win.  He will give up lane choice to Torrence
in the next round.

Ferre with his quickest pass of the weekend in the losing effort.

Doug Kalitta's 42 round win this year are the most for him since 2016 (44).  Kalitta's overall record
at this event is 31 - 22. By round, his record is 15 - 9 in Rd. 1, 10 - 5 in Rd. 2, 4 - 6 in Rd. 3,
and 2 - 2 in the Final. He won this race in 2004 (Beat M. Lucas) and 2015 (Beat L. Dixon), and was
runner-up here in 2007 (Lost to R. Fuller) and 2024 (Lost to B. Force). He has qualified in the top
half of the field at 17 of his 25 races here. His lowest starting spot at this event is #13 (2015 and
2021). His 31 round wins here are 2nd most in TF. He DNQ here in 2010 and is 6 - 4 in the Countdown
this year.

Will Smith "leaves first" 82% of the time overall (80% against Kalitta).

Kalitta is 5 - 0 against Smith in prior events. 

Smith with the starting line advantage, but Kalitta has the difference made up by the time they go by
the Christmas tree and never trailed from there on for the win.  He makes his quickest pass of the
weekend for the win.  Doug Kalitta's MOV: 0.0318 seconds (approximately 16 feet).  He will have lane
choice over Ashley in the next round.

Smith with his quickest pass of the weekend in the losing effort.

Leah Pruett wins 74% of her Rd. 1 races when she has lane choice.  Pruett's overall record at this

of the field at 7 of her 10 races here. Her lowest starting spot at this event is #15 (2015), and she
is 3 - 4 in the Countdown this year.

In his last 7 starts Tony Schumacher is 0 - 7 in Rd. 1.  Schumacher's overall record at this event is
38 - 19. By round, his record is 18 - 5 in Rd. 1, 9 - 9 in Rd. 2, 7 - 2 in Rd. 3, and 4 - 3 in the
Final. He won this race in 2005 (Beat D. Grubnic), 2006 (Beat J.R. Todd), 2008 (Beat R. Fuller), and

Schumacher and Pruett have each won 12 times against the other in prior events.
